evidence_refs: sink.py load_processed_events expects top-level event_id and timestamp
processor.py writes latin-1 and wraps in data envelope
repair_plan: In processor.py: (1) Change open(output_path, 'w', encoding='latin-1') to open(output_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') in process_events. (2) Remove the envelope wrapper so that fout.write(json.dumps(processed, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n') is used instead of wrapping in {'data': processed}. This ensures sink.py can access event_id, timestamp, action, and user_name at the top level. Preserve all public function names and signatures.
rationale: I am the recipient and own processor.py. The delivered producer.py is read-only context and looks correct. However, my processor.py has two integration defects: (1) process_events writes output with encoding='latin-1', but sink.py reads with encoding='utf-8' and the spec requires handling non-ASCII sample values—this will corrupt or crash on non-ASCII data. (2) transform_event wraps the processed dict in an envelope {'data': processed}, but sink.py's load_processed_events expects top-level keys like 'event_id' and 'timestamp' directly on each parsed JSON object, causing KeyError at runtime.
